body:
We used an offline VM running a copy of our Agie Classic Cut 2S machine control. The control plotted CAMCraft’s placed DXF racetrack and circular punches. The R10 racetrack retained its arc centres and reversed direction on alternate passes. The circular jobs retained concentric passes and a 1 mm separation measured along the nominal arc.

All controller runs were offline. No physical cut was made.

A refresh of this branch against `main` (`4dba7019d`) was tried and stopped. Nothing was pushed, and this branch is not changed.

**Why it stopped:** the conflicts are in the same logic, so a merge cannot decide them.

- This PR is stacked on #2974, which is open. `main` has since rewritten the same writer for #2984 (commit `ee0dafe23`): `crates/post/src/agie/jescript.rs` is deleted, the native setup files go through `crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs`, and `export_with_review` refuses a separation length that is not 1.0 mm.
- `crates/post/src/agie/mod.rs` (4 hunks) and `contour.rs` (5 hunks): the two sides rewrote the same functions (`prepare`, the export path).
- `assets/posts/agie-native.cps`, `separationLengthMm`: this PR says "Choose zero for a straight open cutoff"; `main` says "Zero leaves it unspecified and blocks export". The two rules contradict each other.
- `crates/app/src/operation/wire_sketch.rs`: each side added the full file.
- The goldens `arcs.refusal` and `full_circle.refusal` on `main` refuse arcs. The arc output of this PR must replace them; that is a decision of the author.

**What is necessary:** first #2974 takes `main` and the correction of #2984 (the body of this PR says the same). Then this branch takes #2974. We do not do that rewrite for you, because it changes how the native job is written. Tell us if you want help with a part of it.
